{{Quote|The Council sides with the Republic. I respect its wisdom.''"<br />"''Did you ever consider that the Council might be ''wrong''?''"<br />"''No.''"<br />"''I wish I had your certainty.|Agen Kolar and Quinlan Vos|<ref name="Double Blind">[[Republic 54|''Republic'' 54]]</ref>}}
'''Agen Kolar''' was a [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who was known for his [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|skill]] with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and his willingness to use it. An accomplished swordsman who almost always took a blunt approach, Kolar spent many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] traveling the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] on missions. He was intensely loyal to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] and rarely doubted its wisdom or questioned its dictates. When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out, Kolar fought in the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], losing his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Tan Yuster/Legends|Tan Yuster]]. Kolar pushed forward, however, becoming an accomplished [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] and serving in such engagements as the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Clone Wars)|recapture of Brentaal]].

Kolar was also sent on more personal missions, such as his [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (Clone Wars)|attempt]] to arrest the wayward [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Master [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]]&mdash;though unknown to Kolar, Vos was in fact a double agent, and the failed arrest was meant to give him credibility as he attempted to penetrate [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] circle of [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolytes]]&mdash;and the [[Mission to the Rig|show of force]] against the [[Crimson Nova]] chapter of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] when they began taking [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] on Jedi. He also became a member of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], taking on a leadership role in the war.

As the Clone Wars came to a close, Kolar was among the few Jedi Masters remaining on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. When [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] was tracked down and [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|destroyed]] by Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Kolar was among the Council members selected by Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] to confront [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], whom the Jedi feared was under the sway of a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], to lay down his [[Emergency Powers Act/Legends|emergency powers]]. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] revealed that Palpatine was in fact the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] himself leading Kolar, Windu, and fellow Masters [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] and [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] all traveled to [[Showdown on Coruscant|arrest]] Palpatine. Kolar and Tiin were first to perish, launching the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[New Order/Legends|transformation]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Biography==
===The making of a Master===
{{Quote|Agen Kolar. Why is it that every time we meet, you are breaking something? This time it is the customers at my cantina.|Aruk Besadii Aora, to Agen Kolar|<ref name="Double Blind" />}}
[[File:Agenprofileobession.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Jedi Master Agen Kolar]]
A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Agen Kolar was born in the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] rule, hailing from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Iridonia/Legends|Iridonia]].<ref name="H2H" /> After his sensitivity to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] was discovered, he underwent [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] to become a [[Jedi/Legends|member]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="Double Blind" /> By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Kolar held the rank of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and was one of the Order's leading members, known as one of its best swordsmen. At that [[Time/Legends|time]], his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] male, [[Tan Yuster/Legends|Tan Yuster]].<ref name="Databank" /><ref name="ROTS Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

Kolar was frequently assigned to missions across the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], traveling to the edges of Republic authority and beyond. [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] was one area in which he operated, gaining an acquaintance, though hardly friendship, with the [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii kajidic]] [[Lord/Legends|overlord]] [[Aruk Besadii Aora]]. Kolar also partnered with other Jedi on Rim missions, such as Jedi Master [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]]. Kolar gained prominence and respect among the Jedi for his skills and exploits, though his finesse in conducting [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomacy]] was notoriously lacking; he instead preferred to act, aggressively if necessary.<ref name="Databank" /><ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="ROTS Visual Dictionary" />

===The Battle of Geonosis===
[[File:Kolar-Geonosis.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Agen Kolar during the Battle of Geonosis]]
When word reached the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] that [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] had been captured on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] while investigating an [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination plot]] and after having stumbled upon an ominous meeting of the newly formed separatist [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Kolar and Yuster were among the Jedi present at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Both were summoned to follow Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] as part of the [[Jedi assault team/Legends|strike force]] sent to [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|rescue]] Kenobi from the Separatists.<ref name="Attack of the Clones" /><ref name="Databank" />

Kolar and Yuster were among the Jedi who infiltrated the galleries of the [[Petranaki arena]], where Kenobi was to be executed alongside fellow Republic [[Prisoner/Legends|captives]] Padawan [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. On Windu's cue, Kolar and his fellow Jedi revealed themselves in a show of force, but the Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] and former Jedi Master [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] deployed a [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|force]] of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] against the Jedi. Kolar and Yuster battled fiercely, cutting their way onto the arena floor, but numerous Jedi began falling to the massed [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire of the battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. Kolar and Yuster joined a circle of Jedi survivors on the arena floor, but Yuster [[Death/Legends|fell]] in combat among them. When the situation looked most grim, with the few Jedi surrounded by Dooku's [[Army/Legends|army]] of battle droids, [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] arrived at the head of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] reinforcements from the newly-commissioned [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. Kolar was saved and joined the battle against the Separatist armies on-planet, becoming one of the few survivors.<ref name="Attack of the Clones" /><ref name="Databank" />

===Jedi General===
{{Quote|Agen Kolar? Do you live?''"<br />"''At the ''moment'', Master Ti. How many ''more'' moments is ''questionable''.|Shaak Ti and Agen Kolar|<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti">''[[Jedi: Shaak Ti]]''</ref>}}
Kolar was saddened by the loss of his Padawan, but stayed true to the Jedi principle of non-attachment, accepting Yuster's death and moving on. With the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] begun, Kolar was made a [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] in the Grand Army of the Republic.<ref name="Databank" /> Ever a follower of the Council's will and a strong believer in the Jedi's duty to the Republic, he disdained those Jedi who opposed the decision to take an active role in the war.<ref name="Databank" /><ref name="CSWE Kolar">{{CSWECite|II|223&ndash;224|Kolar, Agen}}</ref> When Mace Windu discovered that the esteemed [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] instructor [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]] had [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and joined Dooku's growing ranks of Separatist-allied [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolytes]], he warned Kolar of the betrayal and Bulq's history with [[Form VII/Legends|Vaapad]].<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

[[File:Kolar_MTFBWUA.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Kolar fights for his life in the Battle of Brentaal IV.]]
Five [[Standard month/Legends|months]] into the war, Kolar was assigned to [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Clone Wars)|retake]] [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], a [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] located at a key [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] transit point, from an insurrection led by local clan leader [[Shogar Tok]].<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Kolar, under the command of [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] members [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] and [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]], landed his [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Troop/Legends|troops]] on the planet, but the Republic's intelligence was faulty; Tok's [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]] were operational and shielded, tearing the Republic landing force to pieces. A quarter of the overall forces, along with Jedi [[General/Legends|General]] [[Shon Kon Ray]], were lost almost immediately. Kolar was hard-pressed, though he retained many of his [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]].<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti" />

Ti found sanctuary in a [[Brentaal IV prison|prison]], where she recruited several [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]] to aid her in infiltrating Tok's [[Shogar Tok's fortress|fortress]] via a sewer connection between the two facilities. In order to help her accomplish that, she ordered Kolar to lead an assault on the north face of Tok's citadel. Once she was inside, Koon, commanding the Republic [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of Brentaal IV, would retreat and return in four [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], by which time she hoped to have [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotaged]] the defenses or captured Tok. Kolar, on the surface, was given the option to retreat or surrender.<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti" />

When that time came, Kolar surrendered, along with his troops. He was brought before Tok and the [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] presence of Dooku, who interrogated him as to Ti's whereabouts. Kolar briefly resisted, earning him a [[Torture/Legends|beating]] at Tok's hands, before he testified that he had [[Force sense/Legends|felt]] her die in battle through the Force. Kolar was imprisoned while Tok's forces searched for her body. There he remained until Ti succeeded, at which point he and his troops were freed by two of her recruited prisoners: his old ally, Jedi Master Quinlan Vos; and the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Sagoro Autem]]. Ti was badly wounded after a betrayal by [[Lyshaa|one prisoner]], though, and Kolar took command on the ground in the aftermath while Ti recuperated in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]].<ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti" />

===The pursuit of Quinlan Vos===
{{Quote|You are a Jedi, and the Council has summoned you. Your duty is to obey. Just as it is ''mine'' to make sure you come. Willing, or not.|Agen Kolar, to Quinlan Vos|<ref name="Double Blind" />}}
One month later, Jedi Masters Windu, Yoda, [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]], and [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] decided to use Kolar in a ploy. Vos, already under suspicion of deliberately providing the faulty intelligence for the Battle of Brentaal IV, would be inserted into Dooku's camp of Dark Acolytes as a double agent. However, they needed convincing evidence of Vos's break with the Order. To that end they provided him with high-value military codes which he was to attempt to sell to the Separatists, and the High Council sent Kolar after Vos without the Zabrak Master knowing of Vos's true role.<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="NEC" /> Only that small faction knew the entire scope of what was planned; Kolar was chosen for his unquestioning obedience to the Council and the likelihood Kolar would do his utmost to avoid delivering a killing strike.<ref name="Double Blind" />

Kolar traveled to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] with three clone [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] in plain clothes. As Nar Shaddaa was in Hutt Space, the Republic had no legal grounds to [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (Clone Wars)|arrest]] Vos there, but Kolar hoped to move swiftly and covertly and leave without the Hutts even being aware of a Republic presence. Kolar's troopers raided Vos's attempted sale while he waited outside. Vos fought back, escaping the building, but Kolar [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force-pushed]] him into a wall and drew his lightsaber, capturing him. Vos was manacled and placed in an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] next to Kolar. In his hurry to leave, Kolar allowed Vos's agent, [[Khaleen Hentz/Legends|Khaleen Hentz]], to escape. Vos protested his innocence, maintaining that he was attempting to feed the Separatists false information. Kolar, however, demonstrated that the codes were accurate. During their ride, Kolar and Vos briefly discussed whether the Separatists might have a point, but Kolar insisted that as the Council had chosen to oppose them, the Jedi had no business in supporting the Confederacy.<ref name="Double Blind" />

[[File:Vos_Kolar_Duel.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kolar battles Quinlan Vos in the underbelly of Nar Shaddaa.]]
Their conversation was interrupted by the arrival of Hentz in her own airspeeder. Vos leaped aboard it, and Kolar and his troopers pursued. Vos jumped from Hentz's speeder in flight, hoping to avoid Kolar's notice, but Kolar was not deceived and leaped to follow, ordering his soldiers to continue their pursuit of Hentz. Kolar cornered Vos and [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|engaged]] him in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]], quickly disarming him. Kolar pleaded for Vos to return peacefully with him to Coruscant, where he could find his way back to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]]. The relentless Vos attacked, and Kolar struck back, delivering a warning slice across Vos's shoulder [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to make the point that Vos was outclassed and should submit. Instead, Vos sliced open a cage of amphibians and ran while Kolar dealt with a tide of the creatures.<ref name="Double Blind" />

Kolar pursued Vos through a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] and onto a dead-end walkway just outside it. However, the cantina's patrons knew Vos from his previous undercover work and moved to defend him. When the mob confronted him, Kolar disarmed them with a simple Force-pull. The group was enraged; Kolar deactivated his lightsaber and ordered them to move on or accept the resultant damage. When they charged, Kolar began to engage them in [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]], mowing though their numbers. He was interrupted by the arrival of Aruk the Hutt, who owned the cantina. The Besadii kajidic overlord demanded to know why Kolar was beating his customers; Kolar replied that he was on Republic business. Vos, however, had escaped while Kolar had been occupied. Aruk pressed Kolar to leave, threatening a major diplomatic incident if he persisted. Knowing that pushing the Hutts away from the Republic and possibly into the arms of the Separatists was not worth Vos's capture, Kolar reluctantly allowed himself to be led back to his [[Starship/Legends|ship]] by Besadii guards. One bright spot did remain for the mission: besides preventing the actual sale of the codes, the clone troopers had captured Hentz.<ref name="Double Blind" />

Kolar was debriefed by the Council and sent back to his newly resupplied forces in the field; he transferred Hentz to Coruscant, but was told that it would be fruitless to attempt to pursue Vos further.<ref name="Double Blind" /> Not all of Kolar's time would be spent on the front lines, as he was appointed to the Jedi High Council by sixteen months after the Battle of Geonosis, becoming a part of the decision-making process which he had previously obeyed unquestioningly. Frequently on Coruscant, Kolar received reports of the war's progress along with the other Masters, deciding as much as acting.<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Dead Ends">[[Republic 61|''Republic'' 61]]</ref>

===Sending a message===
{{Quote|He would not have been ''able'' to do this if I had not ''failed'' when I went to bring him in&hellip;!|Agen Kolar, speaking of Quinlan Vos's execution of Kh'aris Fenn|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Show of Force">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Show of Force]]''</ref>}}
[[File:BunchaJedi-Rep65.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Kolar, Mace Windu, Saesee Tiin, and Kit Fisto prepare to take The Rig.]]
After [[20 BBY/Legends|seventeen months]] of war, a new threat emerged: the [[Crimson Nova]] chapter of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] had begun accepting [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] on Jedi. Windu decided that with a few Jedi, he would be able to make a potent show of force and send the message that such action would not be tolerated. Windu recruited Kolar, along with Council members [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] and [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], to travel to [[The Rig]], the [[Space station/Legends|spaceborne headquarters]] of the Crimson Nova chapter, and [[Mission to the Rig|dismantle]] their operations.<ref name="Show of Force 1">[[Republic 65|''Republic'' 65]]</ref>

Windu announced his visit and apparently arrived alone, keeping the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]' focus firmly on him as he demanded that [[Mika (Farghul)|Mika]], the head of the chapter, put an end to the bounties and surrender into his custody. Meanwhile, the other three Jedi arrived covertly. Kolar, under the alias "[[Agen Kolar/Legends|Argent Kole]]," posed as a bounty hunter, with Fisto as his bounty. When The Rig's records naturally failed to find "Kole" among their registered bounty hunters, Kolar railed against poor record-keeping on the Guild's part and demanded his bounty be processed immediately. [[Looie]], the being operating the [[Redemption Center]] desk, was sufficiently intimidated to process Fisto.<ref name="Show of Force 1" />

Fisto escaped from his false [[Binders/Legends|cuffs]] and freed the other bounties, inciting a prison riot. Kolar and the other hunters were denied their bounties until the prisoners were rounded up again, building resentment, which Kolar demagogued into a revolt on the bounty hunters' part as well, leaving The Rig in chaos. With Tiin causing an explosion that destroyed The Rig's supplies and its [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]], Mika vowed to kill Windu. Seeing that no negotiation was forthcoming, Windu reunited with the other Jedi for an assault on The Rig's leadership.<ref name="Show of Force 1" />

In the [[Nest (command center)|Nest]], Mika refused one last chance to surrender. Windu and Fisto engaged Mika and her enforcers while Kolar and Tiin attempted to take the control room. The two cut their way in, where Kolar secured the station's [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]], cutting off reinforcements, and disabled the [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. They also intended to search the files to find out who offered the bounties on Jedi, and may have done so.<ref name="Show of Force 2">[[Republic 66|''Republic'' 66]]</ref>

With that accomplished, the pair set out to reinforce Windu and Fisto, but arrived just after Mika was stunned by her lieutenant [[Stroth]], who could see that Mika's vendetta against the Jedi was against the Crimson Nova chapter's interest. Stroth gave up the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] rebel leader [[Kh'aris Fenn]], who had posted the bounties, to the Jedi. Kolar and the other three Jedi followed Stroth's directions and found Fenn dead in his fortress on the planet [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. Quinlan Vos had left a hologram recording of Fenn's assassination at his hands as a warning from Dooku; after viewing it, the four Jedi came to the conclusion that Vos's fall was a ruse no longer. They believed that among Dooku's Dark Acolytes, Vos's deception had become reality. Kolar blamed himself for not having brought Vos into custody on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="Show of Force 2" />

===Leading the war effort===
{{Quote|We have not the forces to spend on a ''major assault'' on one sentient.|Agen Kolar, rejecting [[Flynn Kybo]]'s proposed mission against Grievous|<ref name="General Grievous 1">[[General Grievous 1|''General Grievous'' 1]]</ref>}}
Kolar continued his role on the Jedi Council, spending time on Coruscant, and aiding that body's deliberations.<ref name="General Grievous 1" /><ref name="Clone Wars 21">{{CW|21}}</ref> In 20 BBY, when the Padawan [[Flynn Kybo]] came before the High Council to request that they approve an assassination mission against General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], the Separatist [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]] and a notorious [[Jedi hunter/Legends|Jedi-killer]], Kolar was among those who opposed Kybo's plan, citing the amount of resources that would be tied up in use against one individual, though it was only later that Kybo clarified that his plan was not assault, but assassination. Kybo eventually undertook the mission without official sanction, proving unsuccessful.<ref name="General Grievous 1" /> Kolar also participated in the discussion regarding the Knighting of Kenobi's Padawan, Anakin Skywalker, suggesting that the young [[Hero With No Fear/Legends|Jedi hero]] had yet to face the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Trial of the Spirit]]. When it was decided to promote Skywalker, Kolar and the rest of the High Council participated in his Knighting ceremony.<ref name="Clone Wars 21" />

[[File:KolarCouncil2-ROTS.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Agen Kolar seated on the Jedi Council]]
Kolar was able to indulge his taste for action as well, taking the field when called upon.<ref name="Clone Wars 22">{{CW|22}}</ref><ref name="Obsession 4">[[Obsession 4|''Obsession'' 4]]</ref> On one such occasion, Kolar and fellow Masters [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] and [[Voolvif Monn]] undertook a [[Battle of unidentified planet (bubble wort projectors)|mission]] to an [[Unidentified icy planet|icy planet]], where they were engaged by [[LM-432 crab droid/Legends|crab droids]] and trapped by their [[Bubble wort projector/Legends|bubble wort projectors]]. However, Skywalker intervened, destroying the droids and freeing the three Jedi. By this time, Kolar had begun using a lightsaber with a red [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|focusing crystal]] instead of a green one,<ref name="Clone Wars 22" /> though he began wielding a blue-bladed lightsaber only a few months later.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />

Another field mission was the [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|Battle of Boz Pity]]. After tips provided by Obi-Wan Kenobi led to the discovery of a significant Separatist presence on the planet [[Boz Pity/Legends|Boz Pity]] some thirty months into the war, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Intervention]]'' was dispatched along with an unusually strong complement of Jedi&mdash;including eight Jedi Council members, among them Kolar. Skywalker was also in the complement, and [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] the ''Intervention'' past the Separatist [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the world, but was unable to avoid a crash landing. On the planet, Kolar and the others made their way to the main [[Boz Pity Confederacy base|Separatist base]], where they found Dooku, Grievous, and the Dark Acolyte [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]]&mdash;all high-value targets.<ref name="Obsession 4" /> Kolar engaged the many [[Squad/Legends|squads]] of battle droids surrounding the fortress, but was never given the opportunity to engage in a lightsaber duel; Dooku dueled Windu and escaped, Grievous killed Master [[Soon Bayts]] before being badly damaged by Windu and forced to retreat, and Ventress was brought down by Dooku's forces after the Count decided to eliminate an unreliable asset.<ref name="Obsession 5">[[Obsession 5|''Obsession'' 5]]</ref>

===Endgame===
{{Quote|It doesn't &hellip; hurt &hellip;|Agen Kolar's last words|<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
A full [[19 BBY/Legends|three years]] after the war began, Grievous [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|struck]] at Coruscant. Kolar took to [[Realspace/Legends|space]], battling against the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] in his [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]. While he was so occupied, Grievous was able to sneak planetside and capture [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] from his [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|offices]]. Kolar, Tiin and Master [[Pablo-Jill/Legends|Pablo-Jill]] were recalled from the battle to attempt to intercept Grievous's [[Tri-wing shuttle|escape shuttle]]. They repeatedly engaged it, but were repelled by debris fields created by Grievous. Grievous could not outmaneuver them as they closed and chewed away at his shields, but he did destroy civilian ships caught in the crossfire any time Kolar or the others got too close, forcing them to fall back.<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Despite Kolar's efforts, Grievous was able to make it to his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]. Shortly thereafter, Skywalker and Kenobi arrived at Coruscant and were able to rescue the Chancellor, kill Dooku, and force Grievous to retreat.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /><ref name="Labyrinth of Evil" />

Kolar remained on Coruscant, serving on the High Council. He supported the Council's request for Skywalker to use his closeness to the Chancellor to [[Spy/Legends|spy]] upon his [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|office]], as the Jedi had grown increasingly suspicious that a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious, was manipulating Palpatine and had in fact manufactured the entire war. Kolar had great faith in Skywalker's abilities, and suggested it was vital that Kenobi, whom Skywalker trusted, be the one to ask him. He also suggested that the Council emphasize that it was stepping up the search for Grievous, which Skywalker would report to Palpatine, hopefully forcing Sidious into action to protect his pawn. He was additionally the one to suggest that, of Yoda or Windu, Yoda be the one to take the field in a ploy to cause Sidious to feel overconfident and draw him into action. Yoda would lead the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|defense]] of the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], Kenobi would put an end to Grievous, and Kolar would remain on Coruscant, along with Windu and several other combat-hardened Masters, ready to counter Sidious.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

[[File:AgenKolarDies-ROTS.jpg|thumb|left|280px|Agen Kolar is struck down by Darth Sidious.]]
When the Council was informed that Kenobi had [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|killed]] Grievous in combat, they moved to confront Palpatine and force him to lay down his [[Emergency Powers Act/Legends|emergency powers]], which he had been accumulating in excess and the Council feared could be used by Palpatine for unsavory ends, now that the war was largely ended. Windu reassembled the same team he had used at The Rig, preparing to lead Kolar, Tiin and Fisto into the Chancellor's office. As they were preparing to depart, however, Skywalker arrived with shocking news: Palpatine had revealed himself to Skywalker as being Darth Sidious; the Republic was being ruled by a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]]. Windu ordered Skywalker to remain in the Temple and set off with the three Masters. Fisto was apprehensive and Kolar wanted to know why Skywalker was not with them. Windu and Tiin were able to reassure them, and the group departed for Palpatine's office at sunset in a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i gunship]], ready to [[Showdown on Coruscant|arrest]] him.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /><ref name="ROTS novel" />

Kolar brought up the rear as the four Jedi Council members strode into Palpatine's office. Each lit their lightsabers as Windu declared Palpatine under arrest. A brief discussion led to Palpatine drawing his lightsaber and leaping across his desk, landing and [[Shiak|stabbing]] Kolar, who was unable to bring his blade into position swiftly enough, through the torso. Kolar died by the Sith Lord's blade, crumpling to the floor as Tiin died in Kolar's last moments.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /><ref name="ROTS novel" /> Fisto was killed shortly later and the duel concluded when Skywalker arrived and intervened&mdash;on the side of the Sith Lord who had manipulated the entire war into being&mdash;Kolar's trust in Skywalker had been misplaced. Sidious killed Windu, made Skywalker his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] and [[New Order/Legends|transformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Declaration of a New Order|declaring]] the Jedi enemies of the state on the basis of the attempted arrest Kolar had helped perform. Kolar and Tiin effectively became the first victims of the subsequent, decades-long [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|If you attack me, I cannot be responsible for what happens to you. I suggest you mind your own business.''"<br />"''Always the ''diplomat'', Agen.|Agen Kolar, to an angry mob, and Quinlan Vos|<ref name="Double Blind" />}}
[[File:AgenKolar-Databank.png|thumb|right|180px|Jedi Master Agen Kolar]]
Jedi Master Agen Kolar was known among the Jedi for his disinterest in diplomatic niceties; he was frequently blunt and often moved directly to action, fighting first and asking questions later.<ref name="Databank" /><ref name="ROTS Visual Dictionary" /> He was confident in his martial abilities, and his idea of diplomacy thus frequently involved ordering an opponent to stand down or face the consequences.<ref name="Double Blind" /> Kolar was known as a stern warrior.<ref name="H2H" />

In spite of these traits, Kolar was generally considered an excellent Jedi&mdash;good enough to gain a seat on the Jedi High Council.<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Dead Ends" /> Kolar was extremely loyal to the dictates of the Council, and did not doubt its wisdom; he trusted it and its decisions completely and unquestioningly.<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Mysteries of the Jedi">''[[Star Wars: Mysteries of the Jedi]]''</ref> Despite that, Kolar was not a silent assenter on the Council, frequently injecting an observation, suggestion, or objection.<ref name="General Grievous 1" /><ref name="Clone Wars 21" /><ref name="ROTS novel" /> It was his belief that the primary duty of the Jedi was to the Republic, and thus supported Jedi involvement in the Clone Wars.<ref name="CSWE Kolar" />

Kolar was moreover a strong believer in the goodness of his fellow Jedi, and had a hard time believing Quinlan Vos, or any other Jedi, could fall to the dark side of the Force. Even when he confronted Vos, he displayed an unwillingness to seriously wound Vos, despite being engaged repeatedly by Vos in combat; Kolar preferred to take a compassionate route with his "brother Jedi" rather than indulge his more aggressive nature.<ref name="Double Blind" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|That could have as easily been your arm. Yield.|Agen Kolar, to Quinlan Vos|<ref name="Double Blind" />}}
Agen Kolar favored the use of Force Push in combat,<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Show of Force 2" /><ref name="Obsession 5" /> and was known to apply it suddenly against his opponents, devastating them with the sheer force of the blast.<ref name="H2H" /> Truly exceptional with a blade, Kolar was one of the most skilled swordsmen in galactic history,<ref name="ROTS Visual Dictionary" /> earning the respect and even admiration of the likes of Mace Windu himself. A considerably talented combatant, Kolar was a master of Form IV Ataru, and was perceived to be second only to Yoda, and rivaled only by Ki-Adi-Mundi in his mastery of the form. Additionally, Kolar was an adept master of Form V and often combined Djem So and Ataru swordplay in his fighting style.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> Kolar's proficiency in lightsaber combat was such that the Jedi Council believed Windu and Kolar alone would provide a significant counter to Darth Sidious were the Sith Lord to reveal himself. Despite the Council's expectations, however, Kolar was slain by Sidious with a single blow, being caught off-guard by the Sith Lord's speed.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

Kolar did not pour his talents in lightsaber combat alone, as he was also highly proficient in unarmed combat, clearly displayed when he engaged an angry mob of cantina patrons on Nar Shaddaa without his lightsaber and without difficulty, being known as one of the Jedi Order's most powerful martial artists. Kolar was thus able to resolve the problem via hand-to-hand combat,<ref name="Double Blind" /> yet without killing or maiming his opponents.<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Show of Force 2" /> Kolar integrated physical combat into his lightsaber battles, being especially fond of delivering high kicks to his foes, though he also favored that attack in fully unarmed combat as well.<ref name="Attack of the Clones" /><ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Show of Force 2" /> In addition to his fighting techniques, Kolar was considered to be a master swordsmith.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
Agen Kolar was originally intended to be Jedi Master [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]], first seen in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']]. As the majority of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] was being shot in Australia, local actor [[Tux Akindoyeni]] was brought in to replace the original actor, [[Hassani Shapi]]. However, Akindoyeni's facial characteristics, skin tone, makeup and hairstyle were all noticeably different from Hassani Shapi's version of the character&mdash;in particular, Shapi's Koth had noticeable lined facial tattoos which Akindoyeni's lacked&mdash;and so Akindoyeni's Eeth Koth was thus deemed an entirely new character: Agen Kolar.<ref name="Databank" /> The newly created Kolar went on to make appearances in the remaining films of the [[prequel trilogy]], [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]<ref name="Attack of the Clones" /> and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the latter of which featured his death during the Showdown on Coruscant.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />

[[File:EethKothAgenKolarAnimated.jpg|thumb|left|130px|Agen Kolar's depiction in ''Star Wars: Clone Wars'' inaccurately resembles Eeth Koth.]]
That change led to multiple instances of confusion between Kolar's and Koth's characters, ones that would last for years. In one error, Kolar's image was used in the entry on Koth in the ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''.<ref name="Power of the Jedi Sourcebook" /> Again, in the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]] of ''Revenge of the Sith'', Kolar was identified as Eeth Koth when Anakin Skywalker attended his first High Council meeting. All subsequent appearances were correctly identified as Agen Kolar.<ref name="ROTS Illustrated Screenplay">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref> ''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]'' also mistakenly identified Kolar in several photo captions.<ref name="The Making of ROTS">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

In one highly visible error, a Zabrak Jedi High Council member that appears in [[Chapter 21 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|two]] [[Chapter 22 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|scenes]] of [[Clone Wars: Season Two|Vol. 2]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' television series was animated with the unmistakable likeness of Koth, but was credited as being Kolar.<ref name="Clone Wars 21" /><ref name="Clone Wars 22" /> Although Koth was originally stated as having been killed at the Battle of Geonosis,<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> this has been [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]]; Koth's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry on [[StarWars.com]] claims that his character design was used in the ''Clone Wars'' microseries,<ref name="Koth Databank">{{DB|character|eethkoth|Koth, Eeth}}</ref> and Koth himself was later featured in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series.<ref name="Grievous Intrigue Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode209.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Grievous Intrigue}}</ref>

Kolar's lightsaber color appeared in ''Revenge of the Sith'' as blue,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> despite having previously been green in all other sources<ref name="Double Blind" /><ref name="Jedi: Shaak Ti" /><ref name="Show of Force 2" /> but one,<ref name="Obsession 5" /> including ''Attack of the Clones''.<ref name="Attack of the Clones" /> It would appear that this was a comparatively last-minute change, as the novelization of the film describes his lightsaber as still producing a green blade and the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic adaptation]] shows a green blade as well.<ref name="ROTS novel" /><ref name="ROTS comic">[[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|''Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith'' comic adaptation]]</ref> The one instance other than ''Revenge of the Sith'' in which Kolar was not shown with a green blade was "Clone Wars Chapter 22," where Kolar appeared with the misattributed likeness of Eeth Koth and a red blade.<ref name="Clone Wars 22" />

In the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Revenge of the Sith'', Kolar was not the first to die. In it, he and Tiin walked to the desk of the Chancellor to arrest him while Masters Windu and Fisto waited at the door. Palpatine caught Tiin off guard and beheaded him, immediately afterward piercing Kolar through the head&mdash;not, as the film showed, the chest. This, as it contradicts the film itself, is considered non-[[canon]].<ref name="ROTS novel" /><ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> Kolar's height is given as 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'',<ref name="H2H" /> but the ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' lists him as being 1.7 meters tall.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> This article attempts to incorporate both statements.

Kolar makes a brief appearance in "[[The Lesson (Star Wars Tales)|The Lesson]]" in [[Star Wars Tales 14|''Star Wars Tales'' 14]], which portrays him fighting in the Petranaki arena during the Battle of Geonosis.<ref name="The Lesson">{{Tales|14|The Lesson (Star Wars Tales)}}</ref> Although several elements of the comic were canonized in [[Leland Chee]]'s blog,<ref name="Geonosis Casualties">{{Blog|holocron|10|Jedi Casualties: Battle of Geonosis}}</ref> the canonicity of the comic as a whole is uncertain.
